From “Berlin desk hedging strategy (confidential)”: We hedge the expected output of our German PPAs with month baseload futures. The target hedge ratio for the front month is 70 to 90 percent of expected PPA output; above 110 percent we are net short and must reduce. Peak futures cover the solar shape only in summer months.

From “Imbalance settlement in Germany (reBAP)”: Every balancing responsible party settles the difference between its schedule and what was actually produced or consumed at the uniform imbalance price, the reBAP. It is set per quarter hour, is the same in all four German control areas and is symmetric: the same price applies whether a party is long or short, except in quarter hours when the capacity reserve is called.

From “EEG section 51 and negative prices (Solarspitzengesetz 2025)”: The 2025 amendment of the Renewable Energy Sources Act (the "Solarspitzengesetz") changed what German renewable plants earn when prices are negative.

From “Day-ahead coupling in 15-minute products”: - Price statistics, negative-price counts and capture prices are computed per quarter hour. An hour with three negative quarter hours counts as 0.75 negative hours, not as one. - Solar ramps are now priced inside the hour: the first and last quarter hours of the solar plateau often differ by more than the hourly average suggests.

From “PPA structures and how we value them”: **Pay-as-produced (PaP).** We buy whatever the plant produces at a fixed strike and sell it in the day-ahead market. We carry price, shape and volume risk. P&L per period is the market value of the delivered volume minus volume times strike.

From “Batteries in the virtual power plant”: The simple rule's share of the optimum tells you how much of the day's spread a basic strategy captures. It falls when days have two price dips (morning and solar midday) that a single cycle cannot both use. Round-trip efficiency matters: a battery at 88 percent needs the discharge price to be well above the charge price before a cycle pays.
